generated_from: the published DAiA/GaC site's architecture-explained.js, architecture-module-inspector.js, architecture-run-model.js and architecture-governance.js, extracted verbatim

retired.request: ADR-168 retired the collection-request step from this deployment; the deadline machinery remains behind a switch. Its explanation is kept so the map can say the step existed rather than silently lose it.

explained.title: Collection request
explained.is_a: A buyer-authorised starting point.
explained.does: Opens a named supplier case and sets the deadline.
explained.matters: Makes responsibility clear before documents arrive.
explained.bound: Only the allowlisted buyer can initiate a case; this is not an invoice approval.

io.title: Collection request
io.purpose: Opens the supplier review and prepares a document request.
io.inputs: Case identifier, supplier and requested billing evidence.
io.outputs: A collection request and a recorded requested state.

obligation.contribution: A defined evidence request makes the case purpose and required material visible before review.
obligation.remaining: A request template does not establish complete deployer instructions or system transparency.

explained.title: Deadline reminders
explained.is_a: A scheduled follow-up step.
explained.does: Prepares reminders before the supplier's deadline.
explained.matters: Makes late or missing documents visible.
explained.bound: Repeatable checkpoints; no live email delivery is demonstrated.

io.title: Deadline reminders
io.purpose: Prepares reminders leading up to the supplier submission deadline.
io.inputs: Collection request and its due date.
io.outputs: Reminder records in the fixture outbox; no real email.

obligation.contribution: Recorded reminders show which collection actions were prepared for the case.
obligation.remaining: Fixture outbox records do not demonstrate delivery, reliable production logging or retention.

explained.title: Supplier intake
explained.is_a: The entry point for invoice data.
explained.does: Checks that submitted information follows a defined structure.
explained.matters: Catches malformed or unwanted data before other checks run.
explained.bound: Typed fields only; the truth of submitted figures is not guaranteed.

io.title: Supplier intake
io.purpose: Receives the submitted workbook and validates the required structure.
io.inputs: Invoice workbook and supporting submission.
io.outputs: Parsed and versioned supplier billing input, or an intake rejection.

obligation.contribution: Rejecting malformed submissions keeps structurally invalid material out of downstream review.
obligation.remaining: Schema validation does not establish model accuracy or training-data governance. Operational invoice fields are not a training dataset.

explained.title: Case history
explained.is_a: A history of invoice versions.
explained.does: Links corrections to the same supplier and case.
explained.matters: Keeps earlier information available when a supplier sends a new version.
explained.bound: Version history exists in the example runner, not permanent storage.

io.title: Case history
io.purpose: Attaches prior submission versions while excluding untrusted free text from decision inputs.
io.inputs: Parsed invoice, previous version and supplier notes.
io.outputs: Case-version context and an input-boundary record.

obligation.contribution: Submission history helps a reviewer distinguish corrected evidence from earlier case versions.
obligation.remaining: Version context alone does not prove complete lifetime logs, access controls or retention safeguards.

explained.title: Invoice checks
explained.is_a: An automatic, rule-based checker.
explained.does: Recalculates amounts and checks totals, periods and attachments.
explained.matters: Uses repeatable rules for facts that do not require subjective judgment.
explained.bound: Limited to implemented checks; an unimplemented rule cannot fail.

io.title: Invoice checks
io.purpose: Applies repeatable invoice validation rules: arithmetic, dates, uniqueness and required reports.
io.inputs: Parsed invoice fields, service lines and attachments.
io.outputs: Individual deterministic pass/fail check results.

obligation.contribution: Explicit arithmetic and completeness checks give review a testable factual baseline.
obligation.remaining: Invoice-rule results do not measure AI accuracy; production thresholds, failure tests and monitoring remain necessary.

explained.title: Contract cross-check
explained.is_a: A comparison with approved business terms.
explained.does: Checks rates, purchase orders, contract scope and spending limits.
explained.matters: Bases review on contract evidence rather than an AI opinion.
explained.bound: Assumes the supplied contract and rate card are correct and current.

io.title: Contract cross-check
io.purpose: Compares the invoice with the approved contract, PO, rate card and limits.
io.inputs: Validated invoice and approved contract snapshot.
io.outputs: Contract-matching pass/fail results and baseline status.

obligation.contribution: Comparison with approved commercial terms constrains which invoice claims can be supported.
obligation.remaining: The reference baseline must itself be current and authorised. Contract matching does not validate overall AI performance.

explained.title: Input sanitiser
explained.is_a: A boundary between supplier text and the review personas.
explained.does: Removes untrusted free-text notes from their inputs.
explained.matters: Prevents supplier instructions from becoming review instructions.
explained.bound: Structural exclusion, not a complete injection detection system.

io.title: Input sanitiser
io.purpose: Defines the trusted-input boundary for supplier text before optional exception review.
io.inputs: Untrusted supplier text and already-validated case facts.
io.outputs: Restricted review input without supplier instructions being treated as authority.

obligation.contribution: A trust boundary prevents supplier narrative from becoming decision authority.
obligation.remaining: A scripted injection fixture illustrates the boundary; live-model attack coverage and security testing remain unproven.

explained.title: Proponent
explained.is_a: An AI-style persona arguing for acceptance.
explained.does: Presents supporting facts, then sends those claims through pre-Judge CoVe.
explained.matters: Balances a critical reading of the case without granting positive claims authority.
explained.bound: Broader workflow verifies both roles; the small supplier fixture does not independently check each positive sentence.

io.title: Proponent
io.purpose: Produces the supportive perspective in a bounded, scripted exception review.
io.inputs: Checked contract facts and case evidence when exception review is invoked.
io.outputs: A recorded supporting argument; not a payment approval.

obligation.contribution: The supportive perspective makes the proposed case for an exception available for review.
obligation.remaining: An AI-style argument is neither verified evidence nor a decision. A second persona alone does not establish effective oversight.

explained.title: Opponent
explained.is_a: An AI-style persona challenging the submission.
explained.does: Raises potential exceptions, sending claims through the same pre-Judge CoVe.
explained.matters: Tests apparently favourable findings with counterarguments.
explained.bound: Claims are provisional until CoVe keeps, revises or drops them.

io.title: Opponent
io.purpose: Challenges the submission and identifies possible unsupported or exceptional claims.
io.inputs: Checked case evidence and the review context.
io.outputs: A challenge or proposed finding requiring verification.

obligation.contribution: A separate challenge surfaces claims for verification before the reviewer receives a recommendation.
obligation.remaining: Scripted disagreement does not prove independence, bias mitigation or comprehensive error detection.

explained.title: Pre-Judge CoVe
explained.is_a: The first evidence-verification gate in the broader validation committee.
explained.does: Checks Proponent AND Opponent claims; contradicted assertions get bounded revision or are dropped.
explained.matters: Keeps both favourable and critical arguments from bypassing independent evidence checking.
explained.bound: The supplier fixture records only an Opponent finding in its smaller verifier, not every Proponent statement.

io.title: Pre-Judge CoVe
io.purpose: Checks proposed findings against supporting evidence before the Judge can use them.
io.inputs: Proponent and Opponent claims plus deterministic case facts.
io.outputs: Verified, revised or rejected claims based on evidence.

obligation.contribution: Checking proposed claims against case facts reduces the path for unsupported findings to reach the Judge.
obligation.remaining: Verification is bounded by available evidence and checker coverage. It cannot guarantee that every claim is correct.

explained.title: Post-Judge CoVe
explained.is_a: A second CoVe gate checking Judge synthesis.
explained.does: Verifies claims newly introduced by Judge, permitting bounded revisions or dropping unsupported assertions.
explained.matters: Prevents final summary prose from bypassing evidence verification.
explained.bound: Present in the broader validation source at pipeline/cove_loop.py; not independently recorded in the supplier fixture.

io.title: Post-Judge CoVe
io.purpose: Represents a further post-Judge verification layer in the broader architecture.
io.inputs: Judge output and the reference evidence.
io.outputs: A further verification result in designs that execute this layer.

obligation.contribution: The broader design places another checking boundary after the Judge summary.
obligation.remaining: Architecture reference only here. No supplier-fixture event demonstrates that this additional layer ran.

explained.title: Judge
explained.is_a: An AI-style persona synthesizing verified arguments.
explained.does: Weighs Proponent and Opponent CoVe survivors, then sends any new conclusions through post-Judge CoVe.
explained.matters: Stops unverified synthesis from entering a human review package.
explained.bound: Post-Judge verification is in the broader source, not separately replayed in supplier fixtures; HITL keeps authority.

io.title: Judge
io.purpose: Summarises verified findings for an authorised reviewer; cannot approve invoices.
io.inputs: Evidence-filtered findings and review context.
io.outputs: A scripted reviewer-facing summary of verified findings.

obligation.contribution: A summary of verified findings helps the reviewer interpret the result while reserving final authority for a person.
obligation.remaining: A summary is not oversight by itself; people still need competence, context and the ability to disregard it.

explained.title: Review package
explained.is_a: The structured handover to a human reviewer.
explained.does: Combines failed rules and verified findings into one package.
explained.matters: Allows decisions to be based on explicit checks and evidence.
explained.bound: A recommendation is not a decision.

io.title: Review package
io.purpose: Collects deterministic results and any supported exception findings for the human gate.
io.inputs: Invoice/contract checks and verified exception findings, when present.
io.outputs: A review package with counted failed checks and verified findings.

obligation.contribution: A consolidated review package keeps factual failures and verified findings available to the human gate.
obligation.remaining: The package supports review; it does not prove that a reviewer understood the limits or avoided automation bias.

explained.title: Supplier correction
explained.is_a: A controlled way to request more information.
explained.does: Prepares a clarification or starts rechecking a corrected invoice.
explained.matters: Gives a safer option than accepting doubtful submissions.
explained.bound: Drafts do not mean emails were sent; corrected documents must be checked again.

io.title: Supplier correction
io.purpose: Prepares supplier clarification or correction requests when the review calls for one.
io.inputs: Findings and missing or inconsistent supporting evidence.
io.outputs: A drafted clarification/correction notice and review status.

obligation.contribution: A correction request gives the supplier a documented route to address missing or inconsistent evidence.
obligation.remaining: An invoice correction loop is a workflow safeguard, not evidence of every legally required remedy or intervention mechanism.

explained.title: Main orchestrator — LangGraph
explained.is_a: The workflow-wide controller: the broader validation process is orchestrated by a LangGraph StateGraph.
explained.does: Routes workflow stages, pauses and resumes HITL, manages corrections and emits ProcessEvents.
explained.matters: Keeps cross-step transitions auditable instead of allowing model-directed routing.
explained.bound: Implemented at validation_workflow/orchestrator.py; the supplier-invoice replay uses separate Python SupplierWorkflow, not LangGraph.

io.title: Workflow orchestrator
io.purpose: Coordinates every recorded case: allowed transitions, routing, reviewer pauses, resumption and corrections. The recorded implementation is SupplierWorkflow; LangGraph is the broader design implementation.
io.inputs: Case request, validated submissions, current workflow state and authorised reviewer decisions.
io.outputs: Updated workflow state, routed checks and review steps, and ordered Event records.

obligation.contribution: SupplierWorkflow coordinates every recorded case through allowed states, deterministic routing and explicit reviewer pauses.
obligation.remaining: The traces evidence this synthetic state machine, not LangGraph execution, durable recovery or production coordination.

explained.title: Human-in-the-loop (HITL)
explained.is_a: An explicit human decision gate.
explained.does: Suspends the workflow until an authorised reviewer approves, rejects or asks for correction.
explained.matters: Keeps final authority with a person, even after all automated checks pass.
explained.bound: Only configured reviewers may resume; hard-check failures cannot be approved. No payment is executed.

io.title: Human-in-the-loop (HITL)
io.purpose: Places final approval, rejection or correction authority with a named human reviewer.
io.inputs: Review package, supporting evidence and the reviewer's response.
io.outputs: Human gate events and a recorded terminal disposition.

obligation.contribution: The human gate separates advisory findings from an authorised reviewer's disposition.
obligation.remaining: Historical fixture decisions do not demonstrate real reviewer training, independent judgment or a production stop mechanism.

explained.title: Committee orchestration — token economics
explained.is_a: A resource guard inside the broader AI committee, bounding model calls, retries and recovery without becoming another verdict stage.
explained.does: Tracks token use and estimated costs, applies configured call/retry budgets and helps enable model fallback or evidence-backed CoVe revisions.
explained.matters: Can recover within a budget without overriding the verification checkpoints or HITL.
explained.bound: Recovery is conditional and not guaranteed; supplier fixture has zero live-model tokens, and the four-proposal limit is not a token budget.

io.title: Committee orchestration · proposal bounds
io.purpose: Bounds scripted proposal contributions and forfeits failed or over-budget adapters. Live token metering and model fallback are broader design features.
io.inputs: Checked submission, scripted proposer and a maximum of four adapter proposals.
io.outputs: Bounded proposals, or no contribution after an adapter failure or exceeded cap.

obligation.contribution: The scripted proposal path limits adapter contributions to four and discards failed or over-budget output before the review package.
obligation.remaining: No direct token-budget obligation is identified in these articles. Live token metering, cost control and model fallback are not demonstrated.

explained.title: Process semantics pool / ProcessEvent stream
explained.is_a: The workflow-wide append-only ProcessEvent stream receiving state changes and process events from across stages.
explained.does: Workflow steps and LangGraph emit typed ProcessEvents to the pool for conformance checking, case continuity and audit.
explained.matters: Provides one history across components, rather than deciding state transitions itself.
explained.bound: The broader source uses validation_workflow/telemetry/emitter.py; supplier fixture instead stores its own in-memory event sequence.

io.title: Workflow event record
io.purpose: Records each SupplierWorkflow action in an ordered immutable Event. State changes add audit.row_appended records; the broader generic ProcessEvent pool is a different implementation of this architectural role.
io.inputs: Workflow actions, allowed state transitions, check results, scripted claims and human decisions.
io.outputs: SupplierWorkflow.events: ordered records with seq, kind, actor, node, detail and source references.

obligation.contribution: Typed supplier Event records distinguish state transitions, check results, claims and human decisions in the recorded workflow.
obligation.remaining: The in-memory supplier log does not demonstrate the separate generic ProcessEvent emitter, durable retention or lifetime production logging.

explained.title: Evidence archive
explained.is_a: A record of the reviewed case and its outcome.
explained.does: Collects the decision and prior workflow events.
explained.matters: Supports later reconstruction and investigation.
explained.bound: Records are in memory; production retention and custody are not demonstrated.

io.title: Evidence archive
io.purpose: Retains the recorded case outcome and audit evidence for inspection.
io.inputs: Recorded decision, rule results and event history.
io.outputs: An archive event; persistence is fixture memory, not a production repository.

obligation.contribution: The recorded outcome and event history provide material for tracing how the case ended.
obligation.remaining: Fixture memory is not a durable audit repository. Production log coverage, custody and retention remain to be demonstrated.

explained.title: Approved contract
explained.is_a: Reference information against which checks are made.
explained.does: Supplies contract, rate card, PO and prior-invoice register inputs.
explained.matters: Makes comparisons measurable.
explained.bound: The example does not validate whether this reference data is current.

io.title: Approved contract
io.purpose: Supplies the reference contract and approved commercial terms used for verification.
io.inputs: Approved contract, purchase-order and rate-card information.
io.outputs: Reference facts for contract cross-check; not necessarily its own trace event.

obligation.contribution: Approved terms provide an independent reference for downstream verification.
obligation.remaining: Indirect support only: a contract document is not an AI control by itself and does not establish Article 10 training-data compliance.

audit.row_appended.label: State transition
audit.row_appended.meaning: Records an allowed change of workflow state.

collection.reminder.label: Collection reminder
collection.reminder.meaning: Prepares a reminder in the fixture outbox; no email is sent.

intake.received.label: Submission received
intake.received.meaning: Records the parsed invoice and its version.

intake.rejected.label: Intake rejection
intake.rejected.meaning: Rejects a payload that fails the typed input boundary.

history.attached.label: Version history
history.attached.meaning: Attaches the previous and current submission versions.

security.input.label: Input boundary
security.input.meaning: Keeps supplier free text outside proposal and decision inputs.

checks.rule.label: Invoice check result
checks.rule.meaning: Records one of the six invoice checks as PASS or FAIL.

contract.snapshot_loaded.label: Reference input
contract.snapshot_loaded.meaning: Loads the approved contract used by the cross-checks.

contract.check.label: Contract check result
contract.check.meaning: Records one of the eight approved-contract checks as PASS or FAIL.

exception.started.label: Exception review
exception.started.meaning: Starts bounded scripted review after the deterministic checks.

committee.proponent.argument.label: Supporting argument
committee.proponent.argument.meaning: Records a scripted supporting claim; it is not a verified fact.

committee.opponent.argument.label: Proposed finding
committee.opponent.argument.meaning: Records a scripted challenge that still requires verification.

committee.adapter_failed.label: Handled adapter failure
committee.adapter_failed.meaning: Discards the failed adapter contribution and continues to the reviewer.

committee.budget_exceeded.label: Proposal guard
committee.budget_exceeded.meaning: Discards every proposal when the four-proposal limit is exceeded.

verification.result.label: Claim verification
verification.result.meaning: Accepts, restates or removes a proposed finding against computed evidence.

committee.judge.argument.label: Review summary
committee.judge.argument.meaning: Packages the verified findings; the Judge cannot approve a case.

review.package.label: Review package
review.package.meaning: Assembles failed checks and verified findings for a human reviewer.

remediation.email.composed.label: Clarification draft
remediation.email.composed.meaning: Drafts a clarification from findings; no real email is sent.

hitl.opened.label: Human review pause
hitl.opened.meaning: Suspends the workflow for an authorised reviewer.

hitl.resumed.label: Human decision
hitl.resumed.meaning: Records the named reviewer decision that resumes the workflow.

workflow.terminal.label: Recorded disposition
workflow.terminal.meaning: Records approval, rejection or a request for supplier changes.

case.archived.label: Archive record
case.archived.meaning: Records the final evidence archive in fixture memory.
